corrections.old_text: Beethoven’s Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67, is recognized especially for its opening motif. Beethoven noted early ideas in autumn 1803 and completed the full score in March 1808. The opening’s four-note idea—three repeated Gs followed by a lower E-flat—has a short-short-short-long rhythm, and Beethoven varies the motif through the work. It is sometimes called the “Fate” Symphony because biographer Anton Schindler attributed the phrase “fate knocks at the door” to Beethoven; Beethoven-Haus Bonn cautions that this account is doubtful. The Fifth and Sixth symphonies were first performed together at Beethoven’s Vienna concert in December 1808.
